items.followUp: A car moving at 25 m s⁻¹ slows uniformly to 10 m s⁻¹ in 3 s. Find its retardation.

rubric.why: The initial velocity, final velocity and time are correctly identified.
rubric.description: States the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying all three values.

rubric.why: Uses a valid equation of motion to find acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent equation.

rubric.why: Substitutes the data correctly into the equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or simplification.

rubric.why: The acceleration is negative, so the retardation is its positive magnitude.
rubric.description: Gives the retardation with correct value and unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 3 m s⁻² as retardation; award 1 mark for obtaining −3 m s⁻² as acceleration but not stating the positive retardation.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 30 m s⁻¹, v = 15 m s⁻¹, t = 5 s.
Formula: a = (v − u) / t.
Substitution: a = (15 − 30) / 5 = −15 / 5 m s⁻².
Therefore, a = −3 m s⁻².
Retardation is the magnitude of acceleration, so retardation = 3 m s⁻².

items.followUp: A force has an x-component of 8 N and a y-component of 6 N. Find its magnitude and direction relative to the positive x-axis.

rubric.why: Correctly identifies the two perpendicular components of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the components as 12 N and 5 N.

rubric.why: Uses the Pythagorean relation for perpendicular components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the components correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution or simplification.

rubric.why: The resultant force has magnitude 13 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 13 N.

rubric.why: The angle is measured from the positive x-axis towards the positive y-component.
rubric.description: Gives the direction of the resultant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 22.6° above the positive x-axis, or an equivalent inverse-tangent calculation.

modelAnswer: Given: Fₓ = 12 N and Fᵧ = 5 N.
Magnitude: F = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²).
Substitution: F = √(12² + 5²) N = √169 N.
Therefore, F = 13 N.
Direction: θ = tan⁻¹(Fᵧ/Fₓ) = tan⁻¹(5/12) ≈ 22.6° above the positive x-axis.

items.followUp: Write any two differences between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in a body.
rubric.description: Gives a valid difference about what mass represents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mass measures the amount of matter, contrasted with weight as a force due to gravity.

rubric.why: Any one further correct contrast distinguishes mass and weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast such as units, scalar/vector nature, or constancy/variation with gravitational field.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on the body.
Mass is measured in kilograms (kg), whereas weight is measured in newtons (N).

items.followUp: What are prefixes in measurement? Give one example of a multiple and one example of a submultiple.

rubric.why: A prefix is written before a unit to indicate a multiple or submultiple of that unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea that prefixes placed before units denote multiples or submultiples.

rubric.why: Correct prefix examples demonstrate how prefixes represent powers of ten.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples, including their meanings or powers of ten.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are symbols or words written before units to indicate multiples or submultiples of the units.
Examples: kilo (k) = 10³ and milli (m) = 10⁻³.

items.followUp: Define Nuclear Physics and describe what it studies.

rubric.why: Atomic Physics concerns the structure, properties or behaviour of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it studies atoms or their structure/properties/behaviour.

rubric.why: Plasma Physics studies plasma, an ionized gas, and its properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plasma as the subject of study, preferably noting that it is an ionized gas.

modelAnswer: Atomic Physics is the branch of physics that studies the structure, properties and behaviour of atoms.
Plasma Physics is the branch of physics that studies plasma, an ionized gas, and its properties.

items.followUp: Define normal reaction and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Friction opposes relative motion, or the tendency of relative motion, between surfaces in contact.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition involving opposition to relative motion between surfaces in contact.

rubric.why: The SI unit of force, including friction, is the newton.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for newton or N.

modelAnswer: Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion, or tendency of relative motion, between two surfaces in contact.
Its SI unit is the newton (N).

items.followUp: Define acceleration due to gravity and state its approximate value on the surface of Earth.

rubric.why: Gravitational acceleration is the acceleration of a freely falling body due to gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition linking acceleration to gravity.

rubric.why: The approximate value of gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface is 9.8 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 9.8 m s⁻² (or 9.81 m s⁻²).

modelAnswer: Gravitational acceleration is the acceleration acquired by a freely falling body due to the gravitational force of Earth.
Its value at the surface of Earth is approximately 9.8 m s⁻².

items.followUp: Define centrifugal force and write its formula for a body moving in a circle.

rubric.why: Centripetal force is directed towards the centre of the circular path and keeps a body moving in that path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its direction towards the centre and its role in circular motion.

rubric.why: The centripetal-force formula is F = mv²/r.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is the force directed towards the centre of a circular path that keeps a body moving in that path.
Its formula is F = mv²/r.
